constraints.statement: The candidate selection is S_Delta = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Delta) }. Requirements-to-test links alone cannot establish complete impact. Exclusion requires supported dependency coverage and a reason the change cannot invalidate reuse; missing edges prove no non-influence. Unknown impact widens assessment or leaves assurance unresolved. New obligations and uncovered cases require work even without existing checks; mandatory gates remain applicable. Selection produces no execution evidence. Selection considers impact analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together, distinguishes estimates from measurements, and remains constrained by required assurance, risk policy and gates; cheap selection cannot leave required obligations uncovered. Broad/uncertain impact, a changed selection model, release rules or missed dependencies can justify wider testing. Full suites can still have gaps; no universal cadence or gate exemption follows. Failures enter diagnosis and authorized response; evidence acquisition may precede justified repair.

conditions: Evidence is reused for a new subject and basis.

the former failure a success nor erases it. The changed subject is assessed
against its current obligations with the applicable evidence.

constraints.statement: E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed, including new obligations and mandatory gates. Retention establishes continued claim/scope applicability, justified assertion/observation bases, required independence, and unchanged material dependencies or an established preservation relation. The original record keeps its original subject; applicability permits use for the new claim. Changed digests prove neither invalidity nor equivalence; changed support reopens reliance, not historical observation. Keep failures, unresolved coverage and citations visible until supported repair, reassessment or authorized obligation change disposes their outstanding status, retaining original observation, counterexample, subject, citations and applicability-change reason. Requirement changes revisit dependent expectations under change authority; refinement changes revisit requirement/realization links; realization changes revisit implementation/integration under remaining obligations. Dependencies are semantic, not file boundaries. Recovery acquires current reality and invalidates affected reliance without erasing valid work or rerunning every check. Role, conversation, component or resumption boundaries alone do not invalidate. Account completeness differs from freshness of every execution.

conditions: Acquiring context for a bound activation.
exceptions: Irrelevant material may be acquired when needed to establish irrelevance.

grounding.quote:
A rule packet without its current subject is
insufficient. A digest without accessible meaning is insufficient. A summary
without supported freshness cannot override its owner. Absence from a partial
projection, sparse checkout or empty local record is not evidence of absence
in the bound subject; acquire its authoritative source or retain indeterminacy.

constraints.statement: Acquisition observes the actually bound subject/basis, including selected frozen snapshots, and binds current task, destination constraints, authority, observations and known material dependencies directly or through declared available inputs. Exclude irrelevant material subject to the stated exception. Contrary admissible current evidence reopens claims under drift/re-entry rules without silently changing basis. Observations correct stale beliefs without authorizing requirements to be changed to fit implementation. Existence and obligation remain distinct. Rule-only packets, meaning-inaccessible digests and unsupported-freshness summaries are insufficient; partial-local absence requires authoritative acquisition or retained indeterminacy. Execution binding declares resource envelope and measurement boundary: bytes/tokens establish fit only for measured context; actual use establishes sufficient relevant attention under those conditions. Fit does not prove attention adequacy, success does not measure unseen context, and no universal attention score follows.

conditions: Observing, resuming or repeating an operation.
exceptions: An already granted operation may be retried when idempotence is established for that subject and effect.

grounding.quote:
Before repeating an operation with uncertain effects, observe or reconcile
sufficiently to decide the next dependent action. A granted idempotent operation
may be retried where its idempotence is established for that subject and effect.
Otherwise select another permitted action or return the unresolved result.
A workspace that retains partial progress does not make every operation
idempotent. An event log may support observation, audit or domain-specific
reconstruction; it is not universally the work state or a compulsory recovery
algorithm.

constraints.statement: Observations bind source and time/version. If subject change between observation and effect is possible, binding supplies freshness/concurrency handling by re-observation, revision comparison, protected snapshot or uncertainty; stale reads cannot be assumed current and no universal isolation scheme follows. The cycle acquires current state, performs a bounded authorized operation, observes its result under the result algebra, and reacquires. It may stop after any operation without completion. Discarded private context is reconstructed sufficiently from workspace and authoritative inputs, preserving progress without requiring every activation transcript. Reuse applies change-impact retention to current subject, basis and changes; green labels prove no validity. Production/invalidation of relied-on support stay recoverable; private context or resumption alone proves neither applicability nor invalidity. Before an uncertain-effect repeat, observe/reconcile sufficiently, apply the idempotence exception, select another permitted action or return unresolved. Partial progress does not imply idempotence; event logs are optional support, not universal state or recovery algorithms.

grounding.quote:
Decomposition, delegation, concurrent work and
recursive application preserve all affected outer obligations and the material
joins between parts. Local success establishes the outer outcome only
when the required coverage and preservation argument hold.

constraints.statement: Intent, Product and Specification refine Z under their owners. Applicable declared calculi constrain lawful transformations but neither select Z nor establish satisfaction; lawfulness proves neither delivery nor optimality. Each transition binds preconditions, permitted effects, result predicate and outer obligations. When finite context/attention prevents one adequate activation, refine into supported transitions. Specification, observation and causal/predictive models have distinct adequacy purposes: accurate prediction proves no required outcome and prediction error alone proves no outcome failure. Paths may be discovered through construction/evaluation. Purpose selects outcome, identity identifies work, and compatibility/assurance determine composition; these premises do not follow merely from finite capacity. Detail/state variation must remain permitted; decomposition, delegation, concurrency and recursion preserve every affected outer obligation and material join. Local success establishes an outer outcome only with required coverage and preservation argument.

grounding.quote:
The actor exercising admitted work authority selects the strategy; a claim
of superiority states its objectives, comparison and assumptions.
The selected design or work record carries the rationale; no exhaustive
optimisation, scalar cost, numerical quota or preferred strategy is imposed.
[Risk and assurance selection](#risk-and-assurance-selection) constrains the
assurance chosen within that strategy.

constraints.statement: Strategy arranges admissible construction/assurance within Z and resource envelope. Its recorded material rationale accounts for context, attention, time, effort, computation, communication and other relevant costs, feedback delay, uncertainty, integration exposure and expected rework, including planning/checking/coordination costs. Justifying measures state units, boundaries and composition, separating estimates, assumptions and observations. Objectives may be incomparable; owners decide tradeoffs. Strategy names prove no superiority; admitted work authority selects strategy, with superiority claims stating objectives, comparison and assumptions. Risk/assurance policy constrains choice. Feedback observes, compares required conditions, diagnoses discrepancy, selects authorized response, acts and observes. Distinguish defective realization, inadequate requirement/design, inaccurate prediction and insufficient observation; preserve unresolved alternatives and allow evidence acquisition before repair. Route supported correction to its owner, preserving counterexample and unaffected work. Changed governing models neither repair realization automatically nor prove former Z reached. Homeostasis guarantees neither convergence nor adequate requirements. Bugs are feature/change work; intake labels grant neither cause, repair class nor authority. Bug lists project existing work. Severity expresses consequence; priority orders response under outcomes, dependencies, resources and authority, separately from semantic result and disposition.
constraints.uncertainty: Spec intake and additional risk policy are referenced but not supplied in full.

grounding.quote:
Completion needs the required evidence and
acceptance conditions on the current candidate. Changing Z follows its owner
and cannot establish that the old destination was reached. Repeating a failed
relation needs a supported causal change; elapsed activity is no repair.
Exhausting a limit proves neither completion nor impossibility.

constraints.statement: Selected control handles admitted states including unavailable input, unknown conditions, failed preconditions, partial effects, exhausted capability and revoked/exhausted authority. Outcomes use the core result algebra; continuation, repair, recovery, re-entry, refusal, yielding and termination remain under actual grants. A selected total control contract responds to every admitted state, without making every operation total or promising universal solutions/external termination. Deterministic, probabilistic and human operations retain selected outcome models; enclosing control reports observed results truthfully. Progress, preservation, termination and outcome satisfaction are distinct. Induction/termination claims require premises and arguments, but beginning admitted bounded work requires no universal termination proof. Continuing work needs supported strategic purpose, possibly bounded hypothesis or uncertainty reduction; discovery may enlarge the frontier, and counts alone are not distance. Lawful stopping need not complete work. Completion requires current-candidate evidence and acceptance conditions. Only the owner changes Z; doing so does not reach former Z. Repeating failure needs supported causal change. Limits prove neither completion nor impossibility. Maintenance may continue under mandate; delivery needs completion conditions. New observations reopen affected claims through retention; recovery reacquires context before dependent action. No role sequence or orchestration runtime is prescribed.

grounding.quote:
Every allocation and reconfiguration, fixed or adaptive, preserves material
dependencies, outstanding obligations, observed and uncertain effects, admitted
authority and required independence. A claim that one arrangement is optimal names its
objective, constraints, comparison scope and evidence.

constraints.statement: Allocation assigns effects only within grants the allocator holds and may delegate. Its rationale covers operations, dependencies, capabilities, assurance, resource limits and failure assumptions; finite context/attention, fallibility and communication costs constrain without deriving hierarchy or fixed roles. Apply actual grants and required review/independence even where one actor performs several responsibilities. The optional Executive arrangement specializes longer-term delivery through bounded worker results, retaining its own grants/procedure. Every fixed/adaptive allocation and reconfiguration preserves material dependencies, outstanding obligations, observed/uncertain effects, admitted authority and required independence. Optimality claims state objective, constraints, comparison scope and evidence.
constraints.uncertainty: Executive profile procedure and additional review requirements are outside the supplied text.

conditions: Each row's stated instance premises and selected methodology scope apply.

grounding.quote:
These are conditional arguments in the selected methodology domain. The table
neither proves completeness for the world nor selects a universal executor.

constraints.statement: The table retains these conditional arguments and owner choices: (a) Interpretation/representation → Faithful projection, AC-017, RF-017: F2/F4 require source-to-consumer preservation of permission, failure and unresolved meanings; equal syntax or valid maps do not prove fidelity. Source owns meaning; projection selects exactness/admitted approximation and end-to-end bound, without universal encoding/decidability. (b) Purpose/interfaces → UP-013/014: F1/F4 require interfaces to serve selected outer contracts; local success defines neither Product outcome nor its burden. Purpose owner selects adequacy; Spec owns outcome conservation/proportional burden; signatures/resource bounds supply no value choices. (c) Identity/state/evidence → Identity Method/reuse: F3 distinguishes identity/state and F2 observation subject; digests prove selected bytes, not identity/currentness/acceptance. Reuse needs applicable subject/support. Identity Method owns coordinates; domains choose currentness protocols; no Markov/replay claim. (d) Typed composition/orthogonal descriptions → Composition/AC-016: F4 compatible joins and F2 model/meaning distinction prevent local conformance proving composition or regrouping licensing reordered/parallel effects. Categorical claims require objects, equality, identities and composition proof; composite owner chooses predicate/loss, execution supplies independence equations, claimant demonstrates them; matching outputs are insufficient. (e) Judgment/authority → Bind, Contract application, Dispose: F2/F6 and actual grant separate evidence, capability, role and permission; delegation preserves limits and owner decisions differ from evaluations. Existing owners choose grants/reserved decisions; domains add identities/limits; no actor/profile is appointed. (f) Independent assessment → Evaluate, Ticket UP-007, Spec assessment/reuse: under a required independent-assurance boundary, F2/F6 bind actual support/assessor; adopted contributions defeat nonauthor claims on those contributions, but counterexamples alone need not, and unaffected evidence retains scope. Governing contracts choose separation/disclosure; domains retain exposure/trace/promotion; no universal count, model family or added stage. (g) Result algebra → RF-012/Evaluate: F1 predicate, F2/F6 evidence and F3/F5 interruption/effects permit completed effects with failed outcomes, performed undecidable evaluation and counterevidence without invented performance. This member selects five verdicts and separate performance/effect coordinates; domains choose admissible evidence/boundaries. (h) Domain refinement → Work result/RF-012/Dispose: F2/F6 preserve reason-qualified domain meaning and mandate; candidate_ready proves availability only; reasonless refined labels prove no fitness/acceptance, and disposition is a separate predicate. Domain owns outcomes/predicates/total reason-sensitive mapping; mandate owner selects dispositions. (i) Result conjunction → Conjoin/frame conjunction/coverage: F2/F4/F6 preserve required slots, failures and effect joins; failure survives missing coverage, received results cannot remove absent required slots, and pure combination cannot prove composite effect absence. This member chooses precedence/normalized-effect join; applicability owners choose coverage; other operators need their own predicate/proof. (j) Workspace → Acquire/recovery/resumption: F3 persistence, F2 revisability and F5 bounded acquisition preserve work through context loss, forbid projection-absence inference and reopen affected reliance while retaining valid progress. Domains select freshness/concurrency/replay; execution selects measurements; fit/use adequacy need separate evidence. Operation owner controls observation/retry/repair and domain idempotence; no universal transaction/reset/retry. Spec owns Product progress/re-entry, control domain bounds handling, Design retains totality preference and grants bound responses; no universal solution. Work authority selects strategy, domains causal models/measurements/risk, requirement owner alone changes requirements; bug labels grant nothing. (n) Construction assurance → Evaluate/Conjoin/testing/closure: F1/F2/F4/F6 limit passes, formulas and combinations to justified claims; consumers bind applicable assurance before reliance. Domains select assurance/evidence; existing result algebra supplies conclusions without added stages/roles/records. (o) Preservation → Composition/complete-transition assessment: F2/F4 with transition, boundary and assumption premises require initial conditions, every step, compatible joins and final implication. Local validity/invariants/sequential arguments prove no unsupported arrival/concurrency/execution conformance. Composite owner chooses properties/loss; execution supports conformance; probability/induction/category claims need separate mathematics. (p) Assertions/observations → Evaluate/oracles/views: F1/F2/F3/F6 with case domain, observation map and checker distinguish necessary from sufficient passes. Observationally indistinguishable differently true cases defeat sound complete decision from that observation alone; favorable runs prove no universal soundness. Source owns meaning; evaluation chooses scope/instrumentation and supports conformance; narrowed scope needs justification, probability/feasibility additional models. (q) Parallel assurance/provenance → independence/combination: F2/F3/F6 with compared paths/shared dependencies distinguish assertion and execution provenance. Execution history does not justify expected predicates; agreement may share error, disagreement needs diagnosis, actor identity/repetition prove no upstream independence. Domains select derivations/authorship independence; statistical claims need dependence models; model-validation owners retain purpose/external evidence. (r) Risk/assurance → strategy/testing/acceptance: F1/F2/F6/F5 and, for quantitative instances, supported probability priors/likelihoods/dependence, require applicability and dependence rather than check counts/multiplied miss rates. Numerical posteriors/detection remain model-bounded, not whole-product correctness. Work authority chooses within policy; probability laws, not F1–F6 alone, justify identities; no universal threshold or mandatory quantification. (s) Change impact → recovery/testing/closure reuse: F2/F3/F4/F6 with material changes/supported coverage require justified retention plus actual reassessment, visible failures, new obligations and gates; missing edges cannot exclude work, selection proves no execution, changed hashes prove neither invalidity nor equivalence. Tenant chooses representation/strategy; owners supply obligations/gates/preservation; costs cannot remove assurance. (t) Configuration → RF-009/adopted Baseline: F4/F5/F6 with fallibility/assurance preserve dependencies, independence and capability; finite capacity derives neither one actor, hierarchy nor Executive. Product/profile/tenant selects configuration; adopted profiles retain duties/prohibitions without granting authority.

grounding.quote:
Repeated spellings in different rows are intentional. Equal spelling, index
proximity, a heading, or inclusion in this file creates no identity,
inheritance, import, equivalence, or authority. Resolution follows
`SPEC_METHOD.md#bounded-context-semantic-resolution`; this index supplies no
fallback decision.

constraints.statement: The index contains no semantic definitions and declares no bounded context, concept, import, translation, equivalence, disambiguation or authority. Each row records spelling, owner-declared bounded-context identity and exact owning clause. Clause plus selected release identifies a candidate meaning; the occurrence supplies governed scope. Unresolvable context/clause invalidates that row and the index cannot repair it. Repeated spellings intentionally establish no identity, inheritance, import, equivalence or authority through equality, proximity, headings or membership. Bounded-context semantic resolution governs; no fallback decision is supplied.

conditions: Using an index route or reporting retrieval.

grounding.quote:
Resolution in the selected complete basis
is satisfied; a route established invalid in that basis is falsified. Partial
acquisition that neither resolves the route nor establishes its invalidity, or
ambiguity that bounded-context semantic resolution leaves undecided, is
indeterminate. A concluded ambiguity follows its reason under the core rule;
a demonstrated lack of a required unique owner falsifies route resolution.
An unusable basis is invalid_basis. A route outside the bound evaluation scope
is out_of_frame. Acquiring irrelevant members is no condition of resolution.
Missing reasons follow the core rule. None reports semantic acceptance.

constraints.statement: F2 separates spelling/meaning, F3 binds owner/exact basis and F5 requires sufficient bounded acquisition. Resolve owner in the selected basis and acquire the material clause under Workspace and context; apply bounded-context semantic resolution before concluding route ambiguity. Retrieval uses core results while retaining original locator outcome/reason: resolution in complete selected basis is satisfied; established invalidity or demonstrated lack of required unique owner is falsified; incomplete acquisition without resolution/invalidity, or ambiguity left undecided, is indeterminate; concluded ambiguity is reason-sensitive; unusable basis is invalid_basis; outside bound scope is out_of_frame. Irrelevant-member acquisition is unnecessary. Missing reasons follow the core rule. None is semantic acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The full core missing-reason rule and bounded-context resolution procedure are not supplied.

conditions: Consumers adopt the stated F2, F3, F4 and F6 commitments for subjects, owners, kinds, readers and lifecycles.

grounding.quote:
Transform and composition preserve the admitted identity and authority
relations or use an explicit owning transition. Evaluate checks uniqueness,
kind distinction, parsing, stability and applicable evidence. Dispose remains
an owning decision where elevation, transfer, supersession or retirement is
required. These descriptions use the shared relations without adding a
mandatory identity format, runtime API, actor or workflow stage.

constraints.statement: Preserve subject, owner and kind distinctions through admitted relations. Governing basis/lifecycle qualify authority or applicability only where owners require, not as universal identity fields. Equal representation proves neither identity nor permission; continuing identity proves no current content/evidence. Bind/Acquire recover coordinates and authentic owner; Transform/composition preserve admitted identity/authority or use explicit owning transitions; Evaluate checks uniqueness, kind, parsing, stability and evidence; Dispose remains owner decision for elevation, transfer, supersession or retirement. No mandatory serialization/API/actor/stage follows. Engine, domain and release owners remain distinct; bound ABG defaults do not define generic law. Bare tokens across owners/kinds and shared family/member prefixes prove no equality. Changed coordinates prove neither new objects nor continuity without owning transitions. Regex proves only its parsing contract, not executable grouping, parent identity or authority. Runtime carriage/normalization cannot invent domain grammar or override published decisions. Carrying grants/rulings cannot enlarge subject, scope, role or decision rights or turn proxy identity into human authority/independent review. Reconstruction proves only declared byte/reference checks, not predecessor operativity, derivation, historical acceptance or successor authority; source change invalidates reconstruction until refreshed. Release versions/selectors remain distinct from object identities and consumer adoption.
constraints.uncertainty: Linked transformation contracts and some identity subcontracts are only summarized in the supplied material.

conditions: Verifying historical derivation coordinates.

grounding.quote:
The refusal retains its cause on the affected verification predicate. A
demonstrated duplicate, alteration, incompleteness or absence in the complete
authoritative member set is falsified. Unbound material, lacking an authentic
basis binding, is invalid_basis; material not yet acquired leaves the predicate
indeterminate. Missing reasons or unsupported labels follow the core
missing-reason rule without erasing independently admissible findings.
Absence from a sparse checkout does not establish authoritative absence.

constraints.statement: Material must contain exact historical manifest bytes/digest. Every required member is exact evidence bytes or a declared ordered byte-range projection of successor-owned members with literal reconstruction bytes where needed. Source paths/digests resolve in successor manifest; reconstruction matches historical member digests; recorded semantic-address rule resolves every required fragment. Missing, duplicate, altered, incomplete or unbound material refuses affected verification. Re-entry requires authentic complete material; an installed predecessor gives no exemption or implicit fallback. Refusal retains cause: demonstrated duplicate/alteration/incompleteness/authoritative complete-set absence is falsified; no authentic basis binding is invalid_basis; unacquired material is indeterminate; sparse-checkout absence is not authoritative absence. Missing/unsupported reasons follow core rules without erasing independent findings. Existing publication-manifest digest binds declared evidence membership. Source projections bind exact current digests; changed sources need refreshed material before reuse. Contract application checks member, digest, fragment and unique membership, preserving each result/residual through core conjunction. Successful reconstruction establishes content/reference checks only; historical acceptance, semantic derivation, successor admission, publication and current authority remain separate owned predicates.
constraints.uncertainty: The actual derivation resource, manifests and core missing-reason/conjunction implementation are not supplied; no verification result is asserted.

grounding.quote:
The engine should carry identity safely.

The domain should define semantic identity law for its own constitutional
objects.

constraints.statement: Identity must be scoped, typed, unique and stable enough for its governed purpose. It is not a flat global-string convention; hierarchy/type establish uniqueness. The same literal may be lawful across scopes with differing authority/kind; no single format suffices across products/runtimes. Readability aids recognition but is secondary to uniqueness/stable governed meaning. The engine should carry identity safely and the domain should define semantic identity law for its constitutional objects.

grounding.quote:
- no two live objects of the same kind may share the same identity within the
  same authority scope
- aliasing across scopes must remain explicit
- serialization must preserve enough hierarchy to prevent accidental collision

constraints.statement: Identity must be unique within lawful scope: no two live objects of the same kind share identity within the same authority scope; cross-scope aliases remain explicit; serialization preserves enough hierarchy to prevent accidental collision. Naked strings need not look globally unique.

grounding.quote:
The method must not treat a family id as if it were a concrete requirement id,
or a release version as if it were object identity.

constraints.statement: Identity is typed. Different kinds should not collapse into an undifferentiated identifier space. Illustrative distinct kinds are goal, intent, requirement, requirement_family, acceptance_criterion, scenario, design_decision, graph_function, asset_surface, release, install, run, graph_call, continuation and event. The method must not equate family identifiers with concrete requirement identifiers or release versions with object identity.

grounding.quote:
If an identity changes, the method should make the relationship explicit rather
than silently reusing the old one for a different object.

constraints.statement: Identity should remain stable for its governed lifecycle, without requiring perpetual immutability. It must be stable enough for traceability, comparison, replay, publication and supersession. On identity change, the method should state the relationship explicitly instead of silently reusing the old identity for another object.

grounding.quote:
Identity should be made unique by hierarchy where appropriate.

One useful general model is:

`authority / kind / value / revision`

Not every serialization needs all four visible segments, but the semantic model
should be available.

constraints.statement: Where appropriate, hierarchy should establish uniqueness. authority / kind / value / revision is one useful model; not all four segments need be visible, but the semantic model should be available. Examples distinguish product-authority requirement REQ-F-CAPABILITY-001, requirement_family REQ-F-CAPABILITY, runtime-authority UUID run, and release-authority release 1.0.0-rc.1. Family/member identifiers differ in kind; runtime run_id and domain requirement identifiers differ in semantic category despite string serialization.

grounding.quote:
Those rules should optimize for:

- uniqueness
- replay safety
- event-stream integrity

The engine should not impose domain-specific semantic grammar on domain-owned
objects.

The domain must define:

- which identity kinds exist
- how they are distinguished
- what makes them unique
- how they are parsed or read

The runtime may transport those identities, but it should not silently invent
their meaning.

constraints.statement: Engine generation rules should optimize uniqueness, replay safety and event-stream integrity and should not impose domain grammar. Domains must define existing kinds, their distinctions, uniqueness and parsing/reading. Runtime transport is permitted, but runtime should not silently invent domain meaning.

conditions: Authority is carried, restricted, delegated, projected, adapted or changed.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded
proxy. Proxy actor identity and human-authority identity remain distinct;
graph-native surfaces may project the relation as `F_H`. A proxy grant names
its grantor, actor, subject, scope, permitted and excluded decisions, validity,
delegation rights, revocation, and provenance.

constraints.statement: Apply Judgment and authority to composition, delegation, adapters, projections, wrappers and registries carrying/restricting admitted authority. Silent widening of scope, added roles, increased cardinality and changed kind are prohibited. Elevation, transfer, split, merge, proxy grant, revocation and retirement require explicit authority decision and identifiable basis. Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy, whose actor identity stays distinct from human-authority identity; graph-native F_H projection is permitted. Proxy grants name grantor, actor, subject, scope, allowed/excluded decisions, validity, delegation rights, revocation and provenance. Direct/proxied decisions preserve source, subject, basis, acting identity/mode, scope, change class, disposition and supersession. Recording cannot widen a ruling; proxy authority confers neither independent implementer review nor unrelated runtime/domain authority.

conditions: A derived domain overrides formats or structures for its own kinds.

grounding.quote:
An override is lawful only if it preserves:

- scoped uniqueness
- explicit kind distinction
- deterministic parsing or reading
- non-aliasing between family and member identities
- stable downstream traceability

Overrides must be published in domain authority.

They must not exist only as ad hoc regex assumptions hidden in implementation
code.

constraints.statement: Derived domains may override identity format/structure for their own kinds only while preserving scoped uniqueness, explicit kinds, deterministic parsing/reading, family/member non-aliasing and stable downstream traceability. Overrides must be published in domain authority rather than existing solely as hidden ad hoc regex assumptions.

conditions: Overriding defaults published by the bound ABG realization.

grounding.quote:
The important rule is that identity overrides must be visible in domain
authority, auditable, and recoverable without reverse-engineering regexes from
implementation code.

constraints.statement: Publish overrides in a lawful domain-authority surface, visibly, auditably and recoverably without reverse-engineering implementation regexes. At minimum the domain should publish kinds, serialization/readable forms, uniqueness scope/hierarchy and grouping versus concrete executable/traceable distinctions. Suitable surfaces include PRODUCT.md for kinds/roles, requirements for stability/uniqueness, design/ADRs for parsing/serialization/normalization, and a dedicated IDENTITY.md registry when complexity justifies it.

conditions: Parsing, admitting or reusing identity.
exceptions: Grouping markers, aliases or headings may be first-class identities of their own kind when governing identity law explicitly says so.

grounding.quote:
A demonstrated kind,
uniqueness or coordinate violation is `falsified` on a valid basis; unavailable
decisive evidence is `indeterminate`; an unusable authoritative basis is
`invalid_basis`; a request outside the reader's declared domain is
`out_of_frame`. A check not run retains `not_performed`. Syntactic parsing alone
can satisfy only its syntax predicate, not authenticity, grant validity or
currentness.

constraints.statement: Regex is at most provisional extraction over an independently defined identity law, not a complete model. Parsers must distinguish concrete kinds from grouping labels and must not promote family markers, aliases or headings except under the stated first-class-identity exception. Acceptance criteria/testcases and other subordinate identities must not collapse into requirement identity because their names derive from its token. Domains needing family IDs should publish requirement_family explicitly. Admission returns the shared result on a declared scoped-identity predicate while retaining domain parsing/refusal outcome: valid-basis demonstrated kind/uniqueness/coordinate violation is falsified, unavailable decisive evidence indeterminate, unusable authoritative basis invalid_basis, outside declared reader domain out_of_frame, unrun check not_performed. Syntax satisfaction proves neither authenticity, grant validity nor currentness. Before reuse observe current owner state and invalidators; stable identity preserves no stale content, revoked grant or old observation. Changed coordinates neither establish nor end continuity; owning transition supplies it.

grounding.quote:
The selector's target is determined by publication, independently of the cut's
acceptance. Moving it does not change a consumer's operative basis; consumer
adoption remains the explicit transition owned by the consumer's governing
authority under Release Method.

constraints.statement: The method must distinguish object identity, release identity, publication/revision coordinates and mutable selectors. Publication determines selector target independently of acceptance. Selector movement does not alter a consumer's operative basis; adoption is an explicit transition owned by its governing authority under Release Method.
constraints.uncertainty: Full Release Method mechanics are not supplied.

conditions: Defining or auditing an identity surface.

grounding.quote: If those questions cannot be answered, the identity surface is under-defined.

constraints.statement: Ask which authority owns identity, what kind it denotes, what scope makes it unique, whether stability suits the lifecycle, whether readability is over-trusted, whether parsing unambiguously distinguishes families/members/aliases/revisions, and whether it is runtime, domain or release identity. An inability to answer leaves the surface under-defined.

grounding.quote:
If a project currently relies on those patterns, the first lawful repair is to
contain the immediate bug. The enduring repair is to publish explicit identity
law and move implementations onto it.

constraints.statement: Implementations should prefer typed readers, explicit kinds and source-authority parsing contracts, and avoid broad regex as the real model, silent family/concrete coercion and leakage of engine grammar into domain semantics. Where such patterns already exist, first contain the immediate bug; enduring repair publishes explicit identity law and moves implementations onto it.

conditions: Product-declared ODD scope with lawful activation and consumer-bound realizations.

grounding.quote:
At each published action and evaluation boundary, apply
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) with the
exact selected Product outcome or admitted bounded prerequisite/experiment,
IntentLineage, TargetObligationBinding, published action contract, current
execution basis and consumer-bound authority. Its material dependencies are
the inputs and causal predecessors declared by the constructive loop.
[Constraint surface](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#constraint-surface) bounds the
worker's external obligations while leaving its internal HOW open.

constraints.statement: Availability selects no package, Product meaning or grant; Spec, Design, Frame, Ticket, Release, World Model and UX retain owners/applicability. Every published action/evaluation boundary binds exact outcome or admitted bounded prerequisite/experiment, IntentLineage, TargetObligationBinding, action contract, current execution basis and consumer authority, with declared inputs/causal predecessors. Constraint surfaces bound external obligations while leaving internal HOW open. Graph-native actions, cumulative typed environments, admitted facts and four-function loop specialize shared law without adding generic workflow/API/category-equivalence/hierarchy. Preserve every material input's type/meaning at consumers; last-output-only wiring fails if earlier bindings are needed; environment declarations keep should force. Authority attaches to invoked function-table rows, not actor/shared library/query access; model synthesis gains no next-action/closure authority by producing inputs. Relate current gaps to exact targets/obligations before invocation; Product authority owns outcome changes and bounded experiments, not reprice requests. Require reachable admitted ledger/event support, projection reconciliation and replay-visible decisions; observations/uncertainty enter admitted snapshot before dependent evaluation. An old ledger cannot defeat contrary observation and lost responses prove no absent effects. Decision predicates for seven closure dispositions, typed no-action and replay-visible yield remain separate from fitness; lawful repair can coexist with falsified edges, successful no-action with incompletion, and yield adds no failure class. Outer closure needs evidence and preserved original obligations, even under inner refinement or smaller post-action targets; evaluate_action binds pre-action target/evidence, and authorized deferral changes applicability without fulfillment. Where a product is ODD and world-model-driven:

- `WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` governs world-model semantics, publication, and composition law

If it needs to build one concrete product correctly, it must then read the product-specific method and local authority surfaces.

that cut; mutable source and the moving version-line selector cannot silently
repair, replace, or outrank it. A mismatch is an adoption defect resolved by
selecting and installing one complete released cut, not by mixing source and
installed members.

Project-local copies are optional, not default. Installed bytes must match selected immutable RC; mutable source/selectors cannot silently replace, repair or outrank it. availability can be satisfied by an authenticated produced candidate without
deciding its fitness. F_H assesses the core decision predicate on its exact
mandate. Invalid basis and scope/capability diagnoses, missing reasons,

Automation, runtime resolution or qualification that silently merges them violates the method.

grounding.quote:

conditions: Auditing governed ODD products or evaluating a move not clearly covered by current method.

conformance verdict: the current assessment remains, and its merit and lawful
ratification need their own predicate, evidence and authority.
